DAMGHANI:v1p271/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r10.claim: Ṣabr can mean persisting in something; here it means persisting in worship of the idols.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r10.anchor: على آلهتكم يعني اصبروا على عبادتها واثبتوا كقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r3.claim: Al-malaʾ denotes people whose presence fills hearts and eyes with awe and majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r3.anchor: أن لملأ عبارة عن القوم الذين إذا حضروا في المجلس فإنه تمتلىء القلوب والعيون من مهابتهم وعظمتهم

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r4.claim: “Among them” means Quraysh: they left Abū Ṭālib’s council after Muhammad silenced them with a decisive answer, urging one another to persist.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r4.anchor: أي من قريش انطلقوا عن مجلس أبي طالب

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r5.claim: The common reading has an, while Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads امشوا without it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة امشوا بحذف أن

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r6.claim: The Kashshāf takes أن to mean أي (“that is”) because leaving a debate requires the disputants to speak and confer about what happened.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r6.anchor: قال صاحب : ( الكشاف ) ( أن ) بمعنى أي

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also credited with the wording وانطبق الملأ منهم يمشون.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r7.anchor: ابن عباس : وانطبق الملأ منهم يمشون

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r8.claim: Their instruction means to keep going and persevere, since they saw no way to stop Muhammad’s cause.

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r9.claim: One reading is that Muhammad’s religion is growing without an apparent cause only because God wills it, and none can repel what God wills.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r9.anchor: ظهور دين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس له سبب ظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, they call the affair one of the calamities of time from which they cannot escape.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r10.anchor: أن الأمر كشيء من نوائب الدهر فلا انفكاك لنا منه

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r11.speaker: الفقال
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r11.claim: A third reading is a threat: Muhammad seeks to seize their religion and rule over their property and children.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r11.anchor: قال الفقال هذه كلمة تذكر للتهديد والتخويف

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r4.claim: Rather than heed Muhammad or consider his message, Quraysh's leaders hardened their opposition and agreed to remain steadfast to their gods and religion.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r4.anchor: the leaders of the Quraysh hardened their opposition to him, agreeing to be steadfast to their gods and firm in their own religion.

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r5.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r5.claim: The leaders believed abandoning idol worship would bring famine and distress.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r5.anchor: they believed that if they abandoned the worship of their idols, they would be afflicted with famine and distress (Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.claim: The rejection of revelation by leaders and notables is discussed further at 34:34.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.anchor: Regarding the tendency of leaders and notables to reject revelation, see 34:34c.

STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.speaker: IK, Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.claim: A report says Quraysh leaders complained to Abū Ṭālib; Muhammad asked only that they declare there is no god but God, promising Arab allegiance and non-Arab tribute, and they scoffed and said they would say ten declarations.
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.anchor: They had gone with the Prophet to his uncle and protector, Abū Ṭālib, to complain about the Prophet’s preaching.

BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r1.claim: انطلق means to go away; الملأ means the chiefs rather than any crowd, named for filling eyes with their prestige and hearts with awe.
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r1.anchor: الانطلاق الذهاب والملأ الأشراف لا مطلق الجماعة

BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r2.claim: Twenty-five Quraysh leaders left Abu Talib's gathering after the Prophet silenced them, saw his resolve to prevail in religion, and gave up hope of a compromise through Abu Talib.
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r2.anchor: وذهب الأشراف من قريش وهم خمسة وعشرون عن مجلس أبي طالب بعد ما أسكتهم رسول الله عليه السلام بالجواب الحاضر

BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r3.claim: The particle أن explains the implied speech in their departure: leaving a council where they had conversed necessarily involved speech, here advice among themselves.
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r3.anchor: مفسرة للمقول المدلول عليه بالانطلاق لأن الانطلاق عن مجلس التقاول لا يخلو عن القول

BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r4.claim: Their instruction امشوا means to follow your own way and leave, since there is no benefit in remaining where this man is.
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r4.anchor: سيروا على طريقتكم وامضوا فلا فائدة في مكانة هذا الرجل

BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r5.speaker: المهدوي
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r5.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports that Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt was the one who said امشوا.
BURSEVI:v8p3#2/r5.anchor: وحكى المهدوي أن قائلها عقبة بن أبي معيط

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r1.claim: The chiefs tell one another to remain in worship of their gods and endure the criticism they hear about them.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r1.anchor: واثبتوا على عبادتها متحملين لما تسمعونه في حقها من القدح

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r2.claim: If unbelievers urge one another to persist with idols, believers have still greater reason for steadfast worship and sincere lovers for patience in seeking the Beloved.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r2.anchor: يشير إلى أن الكفار إذا تراضوا فيما بينهم بالصبر على آلهتهم فالمؤمنون أولى بالصبر على عبادة معبودهم

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r3.claim: The clause إن هذا لشيء يراد either explains their command to be patient or gives the reason they must obey it.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r3.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالصبر أو لوجوب الامتثال به

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r4.speaker: أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r4.claim: Abu al-Su'ud reads it as Muhammad's determined plan to establish monotheism and abolish their idols, not a passing remark or a matter to be softened by Abu Talib's intercession.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r4.anchor: ما ذهب إليه المولى أبو السعود في "الإرشاد"

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r5.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r5.claim: Al-Jalalayn takes the phrase to mean a plot aimed at them and a scheme being made against them.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r5.anchor: لأمر يراد بنا ومكر يمكر علينا

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r6.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r6.claim: Sa'di al-Mufti suggests it may mean that their religion is worthy of being sought and firmly held, encouraging the preceding command to patience.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r6.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي : وسنح بالبال أنه يجوز

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r7.claim: Another reported interpretation says Muhammad's opposition and the events threatening them are decreed and unavoidable.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : (بدرستى كه مخالفت محمد باما جيز نيست

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r8.claim: Bursevi proposes that they mean patience in the old religion is required of them and is their strongest defense against Muhammad's mission, as they expect death to overtake him.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r8.anchor: أن الصبر والثبات على عبادة الآلهة التي هي الدين القديم يراد منكم فإنه أقوى ما يدفع به أمر محمد

BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r9.claim: Alternatively, they may regard Muhammad's rising as a danger that must be extinguished before it spreads and prevails.
BURSEVI:v8p3#3/r9.anchor: أو أن شأن محمد لشيء يراد دفعه وإطفاء نائرته بأي وجه كان قبل أن يعلو ويشيع

BURSEVI:v8p4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4/r1.claim: Their repeated gathering to plot against the Prophet shows that they intended harm, but God insisted on bringing His light to completion.
BURSEVI:v8p4/r1.anchor: ودل عليه اجتماعهم على مكره عليه السلام مرارا فأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره

TAB-FULL:v20p21/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r1.claim: The Quraysh chiefs urged people to proceed in their religion and persist in worshipping their gods.

TAB-FULL:v20p21/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r2.claim: The particle أن is accusative in place and attached to انطلقوا, meaning to set out walking and proceeding.
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r2.anchor: في موضع نصب يتعلق انطلقوا بها

TAB-FULL:v20p21/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r3.claim: A reading attributed to Abdullah has the chiefs setting out while walking and saying to persevere with their gods.
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r3.anchor: قراءة عبد الله: «وانطلق الملأ منهم يمشون

TAB-FULL:v20p21/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p21/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the speaker who set out as ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r8.claim: It is also said that those who set out were Quraysh elders, including Abu Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن الملأ الذين انطلقوا نفر من مشيخة قريش

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.claim: Al-Suddī recounts Quraysh elders—Abu Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth—meeting to ask Abu Talib to stop Muhammad's criticism of their gods and leave each side to its worship; they feared Arab reproach if they attacked after his death.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا، فيهم أبو جهل

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.claim: In al-Suddī's account, Muhammad told Abu Talib he called Quraysh to a word by which Arabs would submit and they would rule the non-Arabs; when he said “There is no god but God,” they rejected alternatives, left angrily, and threatened him.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا، فيهم

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.claim: At Abu Talib's deathbed, Muhammad urged him to profess that there is no god but God; Abu Talib declined lest Arabs say he feared death, and stayed with his forefathers' religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا

TAB-FULL:v20p25/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p25/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p25/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse about Quraysh's chiefs setting out was revealed when they went to Abu Talib to discuss the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v20p25/r1.anchor: نزلت حين انطلق أشراف قريش إلى أبي طالب فكلموه في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:38:4-6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r5.claim: The elites' departure after speaking suggests Quraysh's chiefs had gathered with the Prophet to negotiate over his call to monotheism and rejection of idols; their failure accords with reports on the occasion of revelation.
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r5.anchor: نسبة الانطلاق إلى ملإهم وأشرافهم وقولهم ما قالوا يلوح إلى أن أشراف قريش اجتمعوا على النبي

TABATABAI:38:4-6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r6.claim: The wording elides an introductory verb of saying: they left saying to one another, or possibly to their followers, to carry on and remain devoted to their gods.
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r6.anchor: وقوله { أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم } بتقدير القول

TABATABAI:38:4-6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r7.claim: Their exhortation means not to abandon worship of their gods even though the Prophet criticized and disparaged them.
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r7.anchor: ولا تتركوا عبادتها وإن عابها وقدح فيها

TABATABAI:38:4-6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r8.claim: They take the Prophet's call as a means to a natural desire for sovereignty and leadership, like the accusation against Noah's messenger in 23:24.
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r8.anchor: ظاهره أنه إشارة إلى ما يدعو إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ويطلبه وأن مطلوبه شيء يراد بالطبع وهو السيادة والرئاسة

TABATABAI:38:7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:7/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:38:7/r1.claim: One anonymous reading takes the phrase to mean that the Prophet's persistence and firmness show he seeks some great thing; the author finds it weak and inconsistent with the context.
TABATABAI:38:7/r1.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن هذا الذي شاهدناه من إسراره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على ما يطلبه وتصلبه في دينه لشيء عظيم يراد

TABATABAI:38:7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:7/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:38:7/r2.claim: Another anonymous reading treats the event as a calamity destined for them, leaving no option but to persist and endure; the author rejects it as contextually weak.
TABATABAI:38:7/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى أن هذا الأمر لشيء من نوائب الدهر يراد بنا فلا حيلة إلا أن تمشوا وتصبروا

TABATABAI:38:7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:7/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:38:7/r3.claim: A third reading says patience is the virtue required of them in such circumstances; the author says this and similar readings do not fit the context.
TABATABAI:38:7/r3.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن الصبر خلق محمود يراد منا في مثل هذه الموارد

TABRISI:38:6-9/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r1.claim: Intilaq means going away easily; the same root is associated with an open face or good character.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r1.anchor: اللغة: الانطلاق الذهاب بسهولة ومنه طلاقة الوجه والخلق

TABRISI:38:6-9/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r7.claim: An here is explanatory, meaning that is, go.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r7.anchor: أن هذه هي التي تسمى المفسرة بمعنى أي امشوا

TABRISI:38:6-9/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:38:6-9/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj also allows an implied bi, meaning by saying, Go.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون تقديره بأن امشوا

TABRISI:38:6-9/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r9.claim: The nobles leave their gathering at Abu Talib's house, telling one another to persist in worshipping their gods and bear hardship for their religion.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r9.anchor: هذا تمام الحكاية عن الكفار الذي تقدم ذكرهم أي وانطلق الأشراف منهم

TABRISI:38:6-9/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r10.speaker: عقبة بن أبي معيط
TABRISI:38:6-9/r10.claim: A report identifies Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt as the one who said to persist in worship of the gods.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن القائل لذلك عقبة بن أبي معيط

TABRISI:38:6-9/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r11.claim: One explanation is that this is a plot or matter intended against them.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r11.anchor: { لشيء يراد } أي أمر يراد بنا

TABRISI:38:6-9/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r12.claim: Another explanation is that this is corruption in the land, soon to bring destruction and free them of it.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن هذا فساد في الأرض وعن قريب ينزل به الهلاك

TABRISI:38:6-9/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r13.claim: A further explanation is their fear that leaving idol worship would remove blessings or bring hardship, since they believed the idols caused drought and distress.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r13.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا الأمر يراد بنا من زوال نعمة أو نزول شدة

THALABI:v8p178#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178#2/r10.claim: The leaders' command to go means they went to Abu Talib to complain about Muhammad.
THALABI:v8p178#2/r10.anchor: وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا يعني إلى أبي طالب فأشكوا إليه ابن أخيه

THALABI:v8p178#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178#2/r11.claim: Their command to persevere means remaining steadfast in their gods; Thaʿlabi compares it with al-Furqan.
THALABI:v8p178#2/r11.anchor: واصبروا واثبتوا على آلهتكم نظيرها في الفرقان لولا أن صبرنا عليها

THALABI:v8p178#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178#2/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178#2/r12.claim: They mean that some scheme is intended against them.
THALABI:v8p178#2/r12.anchor: إن هذا لشيء يراد أي لأمر يراد بنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r1.claim: The commentators report that Quraysh's elite, distressed when Umar converted and numbering twenty-seven men, complained to Abu Talib about Muhammad; Abu Talib summoned him, and Muhammad invited them to the single confession that there is no god but God, which they rejected by asking for one god instead of many.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: لما أسلم عمر -رضي الله عنه- شق على قريش ذلك وفرح به المؤمنون، فانطلق الملأ منهم من قريش وهم سبعة وعشرون رجلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the nobles as Qurayshi leaders going to Abu Talib.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الأشراف منهم إلى أبي طالب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reads أن امشوا as an instruction meaning: walk or go.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الأشراف منهم إلى أبي طالب. {أن امشوا} قال: معناه: أي امشوا. وتأويله: يقولون امشوا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r5.claim: The grammarians say أن introduces an explanation like أي: their departure itself implies walking, as in an action being paraphrased with explanatory speech.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r5.anchor: قال أهل المعاني (¬5): أن هاهنا بمعنى أي التي للتفسير، وذلك أنه صار انطلاقهم بدلالته على المشي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq's first construction supplies what they said: they were saying to one another, Walk on and hold fast to your gods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r6.anchor: أحدهما وهو ما ذكره أبو إسحاق أن التأويل يقولون امشوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r7.claim: Muqatil says the nobles' instruction was to walk to Abu Talib.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬1): أن امشوا إلى أبي طالب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r8.speaker: الفراء وأبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r8.claim: Al-Farra and Abu Ishaq offer an accusative construction with an omitted preposition, تقديره انطلقوا بأن امشوا; this works if their departure and walking mean leaving Abu Talib, not going to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r8.anchor: وذكر الفراء (¬2) وأبو إسحاق وجها آخر في {أن امشوا} وهو أن في موضع النصب لفقد الخافض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq's account has the leaders leave Abu Talib's meeting, telling one another to disperse while holding to their current religion and patiently maintain their worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r9.anchor: وقد ذكر أبو إسحاق (¬3) هذا فقال: وقص هذه القصة التي ذكرناها في سبب النزول ثم نهضوا وانطلقوا من مجلسهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r10.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r10.claim: Muqatil interprets this as remaining steadfast in worship of their gods, like the phrase in al-Furqan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r10.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬4): يعني واثبتوا على عبادة آلهتكم، كقوله في الفرقان: {لولا أن صبرنا عليها} [الفرقان:42].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r11.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say this means that a plot is intended against them, referring to Umar's conversion and the growth in the Prophet's followers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p154/r11.anchor: قوله تعالى: {إن هذا لشيء يراد} أي: لأمر يراد بنا , يعنون بإسلام عمر وزيادة أصحاب أصحاب -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قاله ابن عباس (¬5) ومقاتل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r9.claim: The chiefs rose from that gathering and urged one another to continue worshipping their gods; they saw Muhammad's call as a plot aimed at them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r9.anchor: نهضوا من مجلسهم ذلك، يقول بعضهم لبعض: { امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

ELMALILI:38:1-14/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r18.claim: Elmalılı renders the elite as rushing off and urging one another to remain steadfast with their gods, calling the matter something desired or intended.
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r18.anchor: İçlerinden o heyet de fırladı şöyle: “İlâhlarınız üzerinde sabr u sebat edin,

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r1.claim: Muhammad’s uncompromising monotheism and rejection of inherited polytheism astonished the pagans; Meccan leaders came to see their traditions, status, and interests threatened.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in, özellikle Allah’ın birliği inancını tâvizsiz bir şekilde savunarak yüzyıllardan gelen çok tanrıcılık inancını reddetmesi, putperestler için “gerçekten şaşılacak bir şey” idi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r2.claim: Hadith, tafsir, and historical accounts say that after ridicule and insults failed, a delegation including Abu Jahl asked Abu Talib to withdraw his protection; Muhammad defended monotheism and invited them to a faith promising a bright future, and they angrily left.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r2.anchor: hadis, tefsir ve tarih kaynaklarında –bazı önemsiz farklılıklarla– anlatıldığına göre Resûlullah’ı durdurmak için o güne kadar uyguladıkları daha çok alay ve hakaret şeklindeki psikolojik baskılarının sonuç vermediğini görünce

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r3.claim: One reported reading takes the leaders’ words to mean that monotheism is Muhammad’s political plan to rule them and make them his dependents, which they will reject.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r3.anchor: Muhammed’in söylediği sözler, bizi çağırdığı tek tanrı inancı, onun üzerimizde hâkimiyet kurup bizi kendisinin uydusu yapmak istediği bir plandır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation treats the situation as a calamity destined by time, from which escape is impossible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r4.anchor: Bu durum, zamanın başımıza açtığı belâlardan biridir; öyle murat edilmiştir, onun için bundan kurtulmamız mümkün değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r5.claim: The authors prefer the reading that the pagans urge one another to hold fast to their religion and defeat Muhammad; this is reflected in their rendering, “That is what is asked of you.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r5.anchor: Sizden istenen ve yapmanız gereken şey, dininize bağlanmaktır; dininize sımsıkı sarılıp Muhammed’i yenilgiye uğratmaktır (Taberî, XXIII, 126; Râzî, XXVI, 178; Zemahşerî, III, 318). Biz meâlimizde bu son yorumu dikkate aldık.

BURHAN:v2p192/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p192/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p192/r11.claim: The elites’ order to persist patiently with their gods is answered that if they persist, the Fire will be their home.

BURHAN:v1p109/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p109/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v1p109/r4.claim: Qur’anic references to patience are generally commendatory, except these passages where the unbelievers’ endurance in clinging to idols is condemned.

BURHAN:v4p225/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p225/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p225/r6.claim: The particle in the leaders' departure is explained as explicative because their departure entails speaking.
BURHAN:v4p225/r6.anchor: فقيل انها مفسرة لان الانطلاق متضمن لمعنى القول

BURHAN:v4p225/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p225/r7.speaker: الخليل
BURHAN:v4p225/r7.claim: Al-Khalil says they went off speaking these words; amshu does not mean walking away but what they said.
BURHAN:v4p225/r7.anchor: وقال الخليل يريدون انهم انطلقوا في الكلام بهذا

BURHAN:v4p225/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p225/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p225/r8.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as setting about speech, making the particle equivalent to the explicit explicative form.
BURHAN:v4p225/r8.anchor: وقيل عبارة عن الاخذ في القول فيكون بمنزلة صريحة

BURHAN:v4p225/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p225/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p225/r9.claim: A further analysis treats the particle as a masdariyya, a source-forming particle.
BURHAN:v4p225/r9.anchor: وقيل مصدرية فان قيل قد جاءت بعد صريح القول

BURHAN:v4p225/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p225/r11.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p225/r11.claim: Al-Saffar rejects the source-form reading: speech cannot take a bare noun unless it is itself the quoted utterance or stands for speech, which does not fit here; an is explicative.
BURHAN:v4p225/r11.anchor: وقال الصفار لاتتصور المصدرية هنا بمعنى إلا عبادة الله

ITQAN:v2p418/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p418/r18.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p418/r18.claim: Ṣabr is generally praiseworthy, but in these phrases it means stubborn endurance in defense of idols and is censured.
ITQAN:v2p418/r18.anchor: وكل صبر فيه محمود إلا ﴿ لولا أن صبرنا عليها ﴾ ﴿ واصبروا على آلهتكم ﴾

SULAMI:v2p183#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p183#3/r1.speaker: عمر
SULAMI:v2p183#3/r1.claim: ʿUmar says God reproaches believers who abandon patience in their religion by citing the unbelievers’ resolve to persist with their gods.
SULAMI:v2p183#3/r1.anchor: قال عمر : لقد وبخ الله عز وجل التاركين للصبر على دينهم بما أخبر عن الكفار بقوله : ﴿ أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم ﴾

ITQAN:v2p452#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r1.claim: An is explanatory after a sentence with a sense of saying and before another sentence; in 38:6 it means their tongues launch into speech, not that their bodies set out to walk.
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r1.anchor: وأن يتأخر عنها جملة وأن يكون في الجملة السابقة معنى القول

ITQAN:v2p452#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r2.claim: The chiefs’ “go on” means persist in following the idols, not ordinary walking.
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r2.anchor: ليس المراد المشي المتعارف بل الاستمرار على المشي

ITQAN:v4p400/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p400/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p400/r3.claim: The chiefs are identified as ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAsi ibn Waʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and al-Aswad ibn Yaʿuth.
ITQAN:v4p400/r3.anchor: سمي منهم عقبة بن أبي معيط وأبو جهل

ITQAN:v4p400/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p400/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p400/r16.claim: The author says his cited work treats the remaining unnamed peoples, animals, places and times in detail.
ITQAN:v4p400/r16.anchor: وأما مبهمات الأقوام والحيوانات والأمكنة والأزمنة ونحو ذلك

TUSTARI:38:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:38:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:38:6/r1.claim: The unbelievers' persistence with their idols is blameworthy patience: remaining in disobedience.
TUSTARI:38:6/r1.anchor: هو الصبر المذموم الذي وبخ الله به الكفار

TUSTARI:38:6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:38:6/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:38:6/r2.claim: Sahl distinguishes patience in obedience, in pain, in suffering, and blameworthy persistence in disobedience.
TUSTARI:38:6/r2.anchor: وقد سمعته يقول: الصبر على أربع مقامات: صبر على الطاعة، وصبر على الألم، وصبر على التألم

KHATTABI:v1p42/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p42/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p42/r5.claim: “Walk on” suits the call to persist in their familiar practice calmly; “go forth” or “set out” would add agitation that conflicts with remaining steadfast and disregarding Muhammad.
KHATTABI:v1p42/r5.anchor: بل المشي في هذا المحل أولى وأشبه بالمعنى , وذلك لأنه إنما قصد به الاستمرار

KHATTABI:v1p42/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p42/r6.speaker: قيل
KHATTABI:v1p42/r6.claim: A further interpretation takes “walking” here as increasing in number and gathering to support their gods, rather than literal walking.
KHATTABI:v1p42/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل المشي هاهنا معناه التوفر في العدد والاجتماع للنصرة دون المشي الذي هو نقل

KHATTABI:v1p37/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p37/r1.claim: Eloquence does not require obscure vocabulary: the Qurʾān’s balanced register combines grandeur with sweetness and ease, while many rare long words are harsh and shunned by rhetoricians.
KHATTABI:v1p37/r1.anchor: فليست الغرابة مما شرطناه في حدود البلاغة , وإنما يكثر وحشي الغريب

KHATTABI:v1p37/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p37/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p37/r4.claim: An objection says ‘walk’ is not the strongest expression here and that ‘proceed’ or ‘go forth’ would sound better.
KHATTABI:v1p37/r4.anchor: والمشي في هذا ليس بأبلغ الكلام , ولو قيل بدل ذلك أن امضوا وانطلقوا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that during Abu Talib’s illness the Prophet asked Quraysh for one word, the declaration of God’s oneness; they objected, and the verses were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: مرض أبو طالب، فجاءت قريش وجاء النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.claim: Commentators recount that Quraysh, upset by Umar’s conversion, asked the Prophet to abandon his God and idols; they rejected his call to affirm one God, and these verses followed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: لما أسلم عمر بن الخطاب شق ذلك على قريش

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p208#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p208#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p208#2/r1.claim: The leaders told one another to leave the Prophet and persist in worship of their idols.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p208#2/r1.anchor: وحكى قولهم: أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

MAJAZ:v1p7/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p7/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p7/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says early Arabs needed no explanation because the Quran came in clear Arabic and uses Arabic grammar, rare expressions, and meanings; he cites 14:4.
MAJAZ:v1p7/r1.anchor: قالوا: إنما أنزل القرآن بلسان عربى مبين، وتصداق ذلك

MAJAZ:v1p7/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p7/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p7/r2.claim: He reads 38:6 as compressed speech: after the elite set out, they advised, called, or otherwise urged one another to walk and persevere.
MAJAZ:v1p7/r2.anchor: ثم اختصر إلى فعلهم وأضمر فيه: وتواصوا أن أمشوا

NAHHAS:v3p454/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p454/r10.claim: أن is accusative with the sense بأن امشوا; الملأ means the nobles.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r10.anchor: أن في موضع نصب والمعنى بأن امشوا والملأ الأشراف

NAHHAS:v3p454/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r11.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p454/r11.claim: Ibn Ishaq names Abu Jahl, the Rabi'a brothers, Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-As ibn Wa'il, and Abu Mu'ayt among chiefs who went to Abu Talib.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r11.anchor: وقد سموا في رواية محمد بن إسحاق أنهم أبو جهل بن هشام وشيبة وعتبة ابنا ربيعة

NAHHAS:v3p454/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r12.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p454/r12.claim: The chiefs sought Abu Talib's intervention; Muhammad called them to one testimony, Abu Jahl offered ten, and they left rejecting one God.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r12.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني أدعوهم إلى كلمة واحدة فقال أبو جهل وعشرا

NAHHAS:v3p454/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p454/r13.claim: Another explanation has nobles telling commoners to persist in worshipping idols.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r13.anchor: وقيل المعنى وانطلق الأشراف منهم فقالوا للعوام

NAHHAS:v3p454/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p454/r14.claim: They mean Muhammad's message is intended to remove blessings from a people and bring calamity.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r14.anchor: أي إن هذا الذي جاء به محمد عليه السلام لشيء يراد به زوال نعم قوم

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r1.claim: أن can be a verbal-noun particle: they departed saying امشوا.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون " أن " مصدرية أي: انطلقوا بقولهم: أن امشوا

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r2.claim: Alternatively أن explains speech implied by انطلقوا; al-Zamakhshari says departing debaters must discuss what happened.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لأن المنطلقين عن مجلس التقاول/ لا بد لهم أن يتكلموا

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r3.claim: Another parse makes أن explain an omitted circumstantial clause, or a verbal noun governed by it.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r3.anchor: وقيل: بل هي مفسرة لجملة محذوفة في محل حال تقديره: وانطلقوا يتحاورون أن امشوا.

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r4.claim: Another view says انطلقوا means launched into speech like انطلق لسانه, so أن explains it directly.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r4.anchor: وقيل: الانطلاق هنا الاندفاع في القول والكلام نحو: انطلق لسانه، فأن مفسرة له من غير تضمين ولا حذف.

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r5.claim: The ordinary meaning is walking; the livestock interpretation is linguistically and contextually wrong.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r5.anchor: والمشي: الظاهر أنه هو المتعارف. وقيل: بل هو دعاء بكثرة الماشية، وهذا فاسد لفظا ومعنى.

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r6.claim: For livestock, Arabic says أمشى الرجل, so the form would require a cut hamza with fatha.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r6.anchor: إنما يقال من هذا المعنى " أمشى الرجل " إذا كثرت ماشيته بالألف أي: صار ذا ماشية

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says امشوا may mean increase or gather, from مشت المرأة, with ماشية as an auspicious word.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r7.anchor: ويجوز أنهم قالوا: امشوا أي: أكثروا واجتمعوا، من مشت المرأة: إذا كثرت ولادتها

SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r8.claim: After pausing at أن, restart امشوا with kasra because its third letter was originally kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:38:6/r8.anchor: وإذا وقف على " أن " وابتدئ بما بعدها فليبتدأ بكسر الهمزة لا بضمها لأن الثالث مكسور تقديرا

ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.claim: When Abu Talib was dying, Quraysh complained of the Prophet; he offered a confession that would win Arab obedience and non-Arab tribute, Abu Jahl mocked the offer, and they left urging one another to cling to their gods.
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.anchor: هذه حكاية عن ملأ من قريش لما مرض أبو طالب المرضة التي مات فيها

ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r1.claim: The phrase means that the leaders set off saying, “Go on.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r1.anchor: معناه أي امشوا، وتأويله يقولون امشوا

ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r2.claim: Alternatively, an may be understood as bi-an: they set off with this saying.
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r2.anchor: ويجوز: وانطلق الملأ منهم بأن امشوا أي بهذا القول

ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n9/r1.claim: The phrase means a thing desired or to be desired, hence a sensible course of action.
ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n9/r1.anchor: Lit., "a thing desired" or "to be desired", i.e., a sensible course of action.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.claim: Like the previous sūrahs in this group, Ṣād is founded on tawḥīd; Quraysh oppose its reminder from arrogance and polytheism and will believe only when it is too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.anchor: Like the previous sūrahs of this group, this sūrah is also based on tawh@īd.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.claim: Verses 1–11 present the Qur’an as a reminder rejected from arrogance, paralleling earlier nations; Quraysh too will believe only after seeing their fate, when faith is useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.anchor: This Qur’ān is a reminder for people; however, because of arrogance and haughtiness they are opposing it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.claim: Quraysh cannot accept a messenger from among themselves, so they call him sorcerer and liar; their leaders rally people to defend idols and ancestral religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.anchor: They are not able to digest the fact that a person from among them, as God’s messenger, should warn them of the fate of polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r5.claim: When people were influenced by the Prophet’s monotheist message, Quraysh leaders would leave and urge others to leave too, avoid listening, and remain devoted to their deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r5.anchor: when at times they saw that people were being influenced by his message, they would walk away from that place

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r6.claim: The leaders present this as the proper course: resist the religion’s effort to make them abandon their ancestral faith and keep worshipping their gods until death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r6.anchor: mean that this is what needs to be done.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r7.claim: They tell the masses that Muhammad seeks to make them forsake the religion of their ancestors, so they must cling to their gods despite his effort.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p481/r7.anchor: the religion preached by this person is an attempt to make them renounce their ancestral religion

NASHR:v1p236/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p236/r8.speaker: قيل
NASHR:v1p236/r8.claim: Other proposed responses are ellipses, supplied as “you have surely been brought” or “it is surely a miracle,” among other possibilities.
NASHR:v1p236/r8.anchor: وقيل: الجواب محذوف تقديره لقد جاءكم، أو أنه لمعجز، أو ما الأمر كما تزعمون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r4.claim: The apparent setting is their departure from Abu Talib's assembly, where they and the Messenger met and complained, as related in the occasion of revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r4.anchor: الظاهر انطلاقهم عن مجلس أبي طالب، حين اجتمعوا هم والرسول عنده وشكوه على ما تقدم في سبب النزول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r5.claim: An omitted يتحاورون is supplied and أن is explanatory; امشوا literally orders them to walk away from that assembly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r5.anchor: ويكون ثم محذوف تقديره: يتحاورون. أن امشوا، وتكون أن مفسرة لذلك المحذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes أن as أي: departure from debate implies that they spoke and consulted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وأن بمعنى أي، لأن المنطلقين عن مجلس التقاول لا بد لهم من أن يتكلموا ويتفاوضوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r7.claim: Another view has the nobles ordering their followers and assistants to leave.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r8.claim: Another analysis makes أن a verbal noun: they departed with the words امشوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون أن مصدرية، أي وانطلقوا بقولهم امشوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r9.claim: If انطلقوا means launching into speech, أن is explanatory and امشوا means continue in your way, not physically walk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r9.anchor: وقيل: الانطلاق هنا الاندفاع في القول والكلام، وأن مفسرة على هذا، والأمر بالمشي لا يراد به نقل الخطا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r10.claim: The gloss امشوا as a prayer for livestock prosperity is weak: that sense requires hamzat al-qaṭʿ and does not fit the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r10.anchor: وقيل: امشوا دعاء بكسب الماشية، قيل: وهو ضعيف، لأنه كان يلزم أن تكون الألف مقطوعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also suggests امشوا means increase and gather, by analogy with a woman bearing many children and the auspicious name الماشية.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أنهم قالوا: امشوا، أي أكثروا واجتمعوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r12.claim: They were told to persevere in worshipping and adhering to their gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r12.anchor: وأمروا بالصبر على الآلهة، أي على عبادتها والتمسك بها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r13.claim: هذا refers to Muhammad's appearance and rise through prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r13.anchor: والإشارة بقوله: إن هذا أي ظهور محمد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r14.claim: They offer four senses: submission is demanded; God intends and decrees it; it is an unavoidable turn of fortune; or their religion is sought to be taken.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r14.anchor: أي يراد منا الانقياد إليه، أو يريده الله ويحكم بإمضائه، فليس فيه إلا الصبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r15.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r15.claim: Al-Qaffal reads the phrase as a threat: the Prophet seeks control over them, their property, and their children rather than establishing religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r15.anchor: وقال القفال: هذه كلمة تذكر للتهديد والتخويف، المعنى: أنه ليس غرضه من هذا القول تقرير للدين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r1.claim: The Quraysh leaders left Abu Talib's gathering after the Prophet rebuked them and they saw his firmness, having lost hope in his uncle's influence; they included Abu Jahl, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abd Yaghuth, and Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r1.anchor: الأشراف من قريش من مجلس أبي طالي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abu Mijlaz that a man at Badr called them women; the Prophet replied they were the elite and recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال : قال رجل يوم بدر ما هم إلا النساء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r3.claim: The apparent reading commands literal walking from the gathering, with explicative an introducing their words; one analysis supplies a suppressed state that the departing leaders were talking.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r3.anchor: الظاهر أنه أمر بالمشي بمعنى نقل الأقدام عن ذلك المجلس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r4.claim: Another analysis needs no ellipsis: leaving a conversation naturally entails discussion among those departing, and context supplies the speech relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r4.anchor: وقيل لا حاجة إلى اعتبار الحذف فإن الإنطلاق عن مجلس التقاول يستلزم عادة تفاوض المنطلقين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r5.claim: Others take departure as a conventional metaphor for launching into speech, or as metaphorical attribution whose original sense is that their tongues set out.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r5.anchor: وقيل الإنطلاق هنا الإندفاع في القول فهو متضمن لمعنى القول بطريق الدلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r6.claim: Some say walk means keep to your established way and persist in your practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r6.anchor: بعضهم : المراد بامشوا سيروا على طريقتكم وداوموا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r7.claim: Another proposal connects imshu to prolific childbirth and abundant livestock, making the phrase an exhortation to multiply and gather.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r7.anchor: وقيل هو من مشت المرأة إذا كثرت ولادتها ومنه الماشية وسميت بذلك لأنها من شأنها كثرة الولادة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r8.claim: A proposal reads the phrase as a blessing for abundant cattle, an honorific opening; al-Alusi calls it erroneous because the verb needs a separating hamza and the sense is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r8.anchor: افتتحوا به كلامهم للتعظيم كما يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r9.claim: They urge one another to persist in worship of their gods and bear the criticism directed at them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r9.anchor: أي اثبتوا على عبادتها متحملين لما تسمعونه في حقها من القدح

ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r10.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v23p166#2/r10.claim: Ibn Masud reads that they left walking, then said be steadfast; the walking clause is circumstantial or independent, and an is analyzed as in the standard reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r1.claim: This clause explains the command to be patient, or the duty to comply, in light of what the chiefs witnessed of the Prophet's firmness in affirming divine unity.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r1.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالصبر أو لوجوب الامتثال به والإشارة إلى ما وقع وشاهدوه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r2.claim: The chiefs say Muhammad intends to carry through the grave project of denying their idols' divinity, without being diverted or softened; they should stop hoping to bend him and persist in worshipping their gods.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r2.anchor: أي إن هذا لشيء عظيم يراد من جهته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إمضاؤه وتنفيذه لا محالة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r3.claim: One view takes this as a calamity of time intended for them, leaving no recourse but to swallow the bitterness of patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الأمر لشيء من نوائب الدهر يراد بنا فلا حيلة إلا تجرع مرارة الصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r4.claim: Another view says his call to monotheism, or his pursuit of leadership over Arabs and non-Arabs, is desired by everyone, though not every wish is fulfilled.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r4.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الذي يدعيه من أمر التوحيد أو يقصده من الرياسة والترفع على العرب والعجم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r5.claim: Another view identifies the threatened thing as their own religion, which is being sought so it can be wrested from them and abolished.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r5.anchor: وقيل : أن هذا أي دينكم يطلب لينتزع منكم ويطرح أو يراد إبطاله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r6.claim: Another view takes the referent to be patience itself, understood from the command: patience is sought because its outcome is praiseworthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r6.anchor: وقيل : الإشارة إلى الصبر المفهوم من ( اصبروا ) أي أن الصبر لشيء مطلوب لأنه محمود العاقبة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r7.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal reads the statement as a threat: Muhammad is supposedly not establishing a religion but seeking power to dispose of their wealth and children as he wishes.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167/r7.anchor: وقال القفال : هذه كلمة تذكر للتهديد والتخويف والمعنى أنه ليس غرضه من هذا القول تقرير الدين

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.claim: Some expressions differ in form and meaning, as جلس and ذهب.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.anchor: فاختلاف اللفظين لاختلاف المعنيين هو نحو جلس وذهب

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.claim: Some expressions differ in form but share a meaning, as ذهب and انطلق; the sūra’s انطلق is an example of this synonymy.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.anchor: اللفظين والمعنى واحد نحو ذهب وانطلق

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنمنكلامهماختلافاللفظينلاخت.claim: A single form can carry different meanings: وجد عليه means to resent someone, whereas وجد can mean to find what was lost.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: In رجل معه رجل قائمين, the dual accusative can describe the man and the definite pronoun in معه together, as if the phrase said معه امرأة قائمين.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: معرفة فأشرك بينهما وكأنه قال معه امرأة قائمين

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: مع امرأة also contains an understood pronoun, though it has no overt marker; قوم مع فلان أجمعون shows the shared construction.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: وليس له في مع امرأة علم إلا بالنية

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: A dual adjective cannot span phrases with incompatible syntactic relations, such as a nominative subject above the house and another man in a separate clause.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: In ما سر أخاك وأحب أبوك الرجلان الصالحان, الرجلان can begin a new sentence in the nominative or be accusative for praise and magnification.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: على الابتداء وتنصبه على المدح والتعظيم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: The accusative in this construction is praise, not a circumstantial accusative; al-Kharnāq’s النازلين and الطيبون illustrate praise in the accusative and nominative.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: على الابتداء وتنصبه على المدح والتعظيم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: An adjective with the definite article cannot function as a ḥāl: مررت بزيد القائم is awkward if القائم is meant to mean قائما.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: الألف واللام فلا يكونان حالا ألبتة لو قلت مررت بزيد

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: Accusative adjectives may express insult, as in الفاسقين الخبيثين, and the speaker may instead begin a new sentence.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: وإن شئت نصبت على الشتم وذلك

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: A shared adjective in عندي غلام وقد أتيت بجارية فارهين cannot modify both nouns, since one cannot combine their different case relations; accusative praise avoids the mismatch.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: Accusative praise here is compared with النازلين and with فيها قائما رجل, both ways of avoiding an impossible shared description.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: فلما كان كذلك صار بمنزلة ما كان معه معرفة من النكرات

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: Al-Khalīl rejects a dual adjective shared between a definite and an indefinite noun, as in ناقة وفصيلها الراتعان; neither noun can take that description with the other.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن الجرين أو الرفعين إذا اختلفا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: Al-Khalīl treats genitives or nominatives formed by different governors as mismatched, so a dual adjective cannot describe both, as in رجل وفي الدار آخر كريمين.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن الجرين أو الرفعين إذا اختلفا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: With nested annexations such as أخوى ابنين, the full construct is one noun and the later genitive does not share the first noun’s case relation; the adjectives cannot cover both levels.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: The same restriction applies to definite nested annexations such as أخوى ابنيك; later adjectives cannot jointly describe both the brothers and sons.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: هذا فرس أخوى ابنيك العقلاء الحلماء

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: After هذان أخواك وقد تولى أبواك, الرجال الصالحون cannot describe the earlier nouns; it must be a new subject or accusative praise.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: نحو هذان أخواك وقد تولى أبواك الرجال الصالحون

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: Al-Khalīl reads مررت بزيد وأتاني أخوه أنفسهما in the nominative as هما صاحباي أنفسهما, or in the accusative as أعنيهما; it is not praise.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن الجرين أو الرفعين إذا اختلفا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: A shared adjective is possible when the two nouns have the same grammatical basis, whether both are subjects or each is raised by its verb.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.claim: A description cannot join someone known with someone not yet established as known: الرجلين الصالحين cannot modify من عبد الله وهذا زيد together.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذارجلمعهرجلقائمين|فهذا.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تخلط من تعلم ومن لا تعلم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r1.claim: After حتى, إنّ can begin an independent clause and is not governed by حتى, just as a nominal sentence follows حتى زيد ذاهب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r1.anchor: فحتى هاهنا معلقة لا تعمل شيئا في إن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r2.claim: Treating حتى أن as a subordinate verbal noun would be unsuitable here: حتى الانطلاق or حتى الخبر would turn the clause into a report, so it is parsed as an initial clause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r2.anchor: فهذا موضع ابتداء وحتى بمنزلة إذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r3.claim: فإذا إنه likewise begins a new clause; the cited verse-like line means فإذا هو عبد القفا واللهازم, while فإذا أنه عبد can instead mean that his state is servitude and baseness.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r4.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl parses حتى أنك أحمق as though one said حتى حمقك, then placed أن in that nominal position.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r4.anchor: حتى حمقك ثم وضعت أن في هذا الموضع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r5.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r5.claim: Al-Khalīl rejects كما أنك on the pattern كما أنت because إن cannot begin every clause; يوم الجمعة إنك ذاهب and كيف إنك صانع are not allowed.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#506/r5.anchor: وسألته هل يجوز كما أنك ههنا على حد قوله كما أنت هاهنا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes أن امشوا in the verse as explanatory أي: they went out saying ‘Go and persevere’, not as saying they went out by walking.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: لأنك إذا قلت انطلق بنو فلان أن امشوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: The same explanatory construction appears in ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله, where أن introduces the content of the command.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: وهذا تفسير الخليل ومثل هذا في القرآن كثير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: In كتبت إليه أن افعل and أمرته أن قم, one analysis makes أن the subjunctive particle linked to an imperative, as الذي links to a verb addressed to the listener.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: كتبت إليه أن افعل وأمرته أن قم فيكون على وجهين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: The ability to add بَـ in أوعزت إليه بأن افعل supports the subjunctive-particle analysis; if أن were أي, the preposition could not attach as it does to nouns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: فلو كانت أي لم تدخلها الباء كما تدخل في الأسماء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: A second analysis of كتبت إليه أن افعل makes أن explanatory أي, like its use after انطلق in the verse.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: والوجه الآخر أن تكون بمنزلة أي كما كانت بمنزلة أي في الأول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: In وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله and أن لا إله إلا الله, أن is heavy with an understood pronoun, as if أنه الحمد لله; it is neither subjunctive أن nor explanatory أي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: أن التي تنصب الفعل لأن تلك لا يبتدأ بعدها الأسماء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: In وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم قد صدقت الرؤيا, the clause means ناديناه أنك قد صدقت الرؤيا يا إبراهيم.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: ناديناه أنك قد صدقت الرؤيا يا إبراهيم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: Al-Khalīl allows the call construction also to be understood as أي; أرسل إليه أن ما أنت وذا is likewise explanatory, while بأنك ما أنت وذا shows the heavy form in use.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: وإذا قلت أرسل إليه أن ما أنت وذا فهي على أي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: For the reading أن غضب الله عليها in the fifth oath, Sībawayh understands heavy أن with its pronoun omitted; it is not light أن before a noun unless that pronoun is intended.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: فكأنه قال أنه غضب الله عليها لا تخففها في الكلام أبدا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: When lightened, أن retains its governing force: poetic كأن وريديه رشاء خلب and أن هالك كل من يحفى وينتعل are understood with the omitted heavy particle and its pronoun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: أن هالك كل من يحفى وينتعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: The poetic nominative كأن وريداه is possible with an understood pronoun, by analogy with إنّه من يأتها تعطه or a clause such as كأن ظبية تعطو.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: وإن شئت رفعت في قول الشاعر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: Sībawayh says treating the lightened construction like إنما or لكن after deleting the pronoun would also be a strong analysis.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: ولو أنهم إذ حذفوا جعلوه بمنزلة إنما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: أن بسم الله is understood as أنه بسم الله because no overt subject has been introduced; the implied pronoun accounts for the construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: لأنك لم تذكر مبتدأ أو مبنيا عليه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.claim: The hidden pronoun is confirmed by the awkwardness of أن يقول ذاك without أن لا or a future marker; if أن were an initial particle, the following verb would be indicative.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهأنبمنزلةأي)#511.anchor: أنك تستقبح قد عرفت أن يقول ذاك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r1.claim: The leaders left the gathering at Abu Talib's and told one another to go and remain steadfast in worship of their gods.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r1.anchor: أي: انطلقوا من مجلسهم الذي كانوا فيه عند أبي طالب، يقول بعضهم لبعض: امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r2.claim: “Be patient over your gods” means to persist in worshipping them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r3.claim: They viewed the Muslims' growing numbers after Umar's conversion as a deliberate plan against them, since his standing strengthened the Muslims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r3.anchor: وذلك أن عمر لما أسلم وحصل للمسلمين قوة بمكانه قالوا: إن هذا الذي نراه من زيادة أصحاب محمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r4.claim: Other explanations are that the plan is intended for the people of earth, or that Muhammad intends to rule over them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72/r4.anchor: وقيل: يراد بأهل الأرض، وقيل: يراد بمحمد أن يملك علينا.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكسرفيهأوائلالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكسرفيهأوائلالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكسرفيهأوائلالأفعالالم.claim: Sībawayh uses انطلق as an inchoative-pattern example: imperfect forms in related derived patterns take kasra in their initial prefixes by analogy with forms beginning with hamzat al-waṣl, although that alif was omitted for ease.

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r1.claim: Quraysh's leading men left Abū Ṭālib's gathering after the Prophet had silenced them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r1.anchor: وانطلق أشراف قريش من مجلس أبي طالب

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r2.claim: An is explanatory because leaving a discussion signals speech; alternatively, inṭilāq means launching into speech itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r2.anchor: هي المفسرة لأن الانطلاق عن مجلس التقاول يشعر بالقول

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r3.claim: One explanation of imshū is “gather together,” like the term for a woman having many children and the word for livestock.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r3.anchor: من مشت المرأة إذا كثرت أولادها ومنه الماشية أي اجتمعوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r4.claim: The verse is also read without an, or with yamshūna an iṣbirū.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r4.anchor: وقرىء بغير { أن } وقرىء «يمشون أن اصبروا»

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r5.claim: The leaders urge one another to remain firm in worshipping their gods, since talking with Muhammad will not help them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r6.claim: They may mean that an unavoidable twist of fate is being directed against them; that monotheism or Muhammad's bid for leadership is something everyone desires; or that their religion is being targeted for seizure.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:6/r6.anchor: إن هذا الأمر لشيء من ريب الزمان يراد بنا فلا مرد له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r6.claim: The group that departed were their chiefs and nobles, explicitly distinguished from their lesser followers and from outsiders.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r6.anchor: وانطلق } ولما كان ما فعلوه : { الملأ } أي الأشراف , وقال : { منهم } أي لا من غيرهم فكيف بالأسقاط منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r7.claim: The departure clause embeds their command to go away; if pausing at an, begin the imperative with kasra from its original form, unlike the feminine form with ḍamma.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r7.anchor: وإذا وقف على ( أن ) ابتدئ بكسر الهمزة لأن أصله : امشيوا فالثالث مكسور كما أنه لو قيل لأمرأة : اغزي يبتدأ بالضم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r8.claim: They urge one another to remain in worship of their gods and not turn toward anything else.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r8.anchor: واصبروا على آلهتكم } أي لزوم عبادتها وعدم الالتفات إلى ما سواها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r9.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r9.claim: Al-Qushayrī draws an exhortation for believers: if disbelievers urge patience with idols, believers have greater reason to persevere in worship and remain steadfast.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r9.anchor: قال القشيري : وإذا تواصى الكفار فيما بينهم بالصبر على آلهتهم فالمؤمنون أولى بالصبر على عبادة معبودهم والاستقامة في دينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r10.claim: Their phrase may mean that the call to persist is something worth desiring and never abandoning, or that the Prophet seeks something they do not understand.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r10.anchor: أي هو أهل للإرادة فهو أهل لئلا ينفك عنه , أو الذي يدعو إليه شيء يريده هو ولا نعلم نحن

DURR-FULL:v7p143/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p143/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p143/r1.claim: The account says Quraysh's leaders asked Abu Talib to make Muhammad stop insulting their gods; Muhammad invited them to affirm God's oneness, rejected every substitute, and they left threatening him and his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p143/r1.anchor: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا: يا أبا طالب أنت كبيرنا وسيدنا فأنصفنا من ابن أخيك

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r2.claim: Abu Majliz reports that when someone at Badr called them only women, the Prophet corrected him: they were the chiefs, and recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r2.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: قال رجل يوم بدر ما هم إلا النساء قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: بل هم الملأ

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed when Quraysh's notables went to Abu Talib to speak about the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وانطلق الملأ منهم} قال: نزلت حين انطلق أشراف قريش

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the leader who departed as Abu Jahl.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {وانطلق الملأ منهم} قال: أبو جهل

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the leader who said to walk away and remain steadfast as ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا واصبروا} قال: هو عقبة بن أبي معيط

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r1.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r1.claim: Abū Mijlaz reports that at Badr a man called the opposing group women; the Prophet corrected him, saying they were the chiefs, and recited this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r1.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال : قال رجل يوم بدر ، ما هم الا النساء قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' بل هم الملا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed when Quraysh’s notables went to Abū Ṭālib to speak to him about the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : وانطلق الملا منهم قال : نزلت حين انطلق اشراف قريش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r1.claim: Intilāq literally means to depart and walk, but also serves as a verb of beginning because a person sets out toward an undertaking; the author compares dhahaba bi-fiʿl and the usage in a cited poem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r1.anchor: ويستعمل استعمال أفعال الشروع لأن الشارع ينطلق إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r2.speaker: النبهاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r2.claim: Al-Nabhānī’s line using dhahaba with a verb illustrates the analogous construction for a verb of beginning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r2.anchor: فإن كنت سيدنا سدتنا وإن كنت للخال فاذهب فخل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r3.claim: The use is compared with qāma in the account of the youths who stood and spoke in Sūrat al-Kahf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r3.anchor: وكذلك قام في قوله تعالى : { إذ قاموا فقالوا في سورة الكهف }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the chiefs actually left Abū Ṭālib’s gathering; he identifies ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ as the speaker.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية : قائل ذلك عقبة بن أبي معيط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r5.speaker: غير ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r5.claim: Other commentators name Abū Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth among those speaking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r5.anchor: وقال غير ابن عطية : إن من القائلين أبا جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r6.claim: An is explanatory: if intilāq is figurative for beginning, the chiefs began speaking; if it is literal departure, their exit after the prior debate implies discussion and planning, which the quoted command explains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r6.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية لأن الانطلاق إن كان مجازا فهو في الشروع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r7.claim: ‘Go on’ may mean literally leave the place of debate and remain firm in worship of your gods, or figuratively continue in your religion, like the idiom ‘walk as the noble walked.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r7.anchor: والأمر بالمشي يحتمل أن يكون حقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r8.claim: Ṣabr is persistence and attachment, originally said of tying an animal; in hardship it means staying composed without panic.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r9.claim: The call to remain steadfast in worship of the gods parallels the people’s claim that the Prophet nearly led them astray had they not persisted in their worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r9.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى : { إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r10.claim: ʿAlā conveys figurative establishment, as in ‘they are upon guidance’; unlike ṣabr ʿalā meaning patience with something, it means adhere to or remain in worship, with an implied noun ‘worship.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p210/r10.anchor: وحرف { على } يدل على تضمين { اصبروا } معنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r1.claim: Their claim that this is a contrived matter meant for some ulterior purpose is intended to strengthen suspicion that the Prophet’s call is false.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r1.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالصبر على آلهتهم لقصد تقوية شكهم في صحة دعوة النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r2.claim: The demonstrative refers to what they heard at the gathering: the Prophet’s call to say there is no god but God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r2.anchor: فالإشارة ب { هاذا } إلى ما كانوا يسمعونه في المجلس من دعوة النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r1.claim: The account says Quraysh's leaders gathered while Abu Talib was ill, fearing that after he died they would harm Muhammad and Arabs would blame them for having waited until his uncle's death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r1.anchor: روي في قصص هذه الآية أن أشراف قريش وجماعتهم اجتمعوا عند مرض أبي طالب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r2.claim: They went to Abu Talib asking him to mediate: Muhammad should worship his God at home, leave their idols alone, and stop confronting them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r2.anchor: فنهضوا إليه، فقالوا يا أبا طالب إن محمدا يسب ويسفه آراءنا وآراء آبائنا ونحن لا نقاره على ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r3.claim: Abu Talib relayed the proposed truce to Muhammad; Muhammad asked for a different offer, then requested a word that would make Arabs submit and foreigners pay jizya. When he named the profession that there is no god but God, they refused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r3.anchor: فقال: أو غير ذلك يا عم؟ قال وما هو؟ قال: يعطوني كلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r4.claim: Some of the departing leaders repeated the objection that he would make the gods one, while Uqbah ibn Abi Muayt told them to go on and persevere in their gods.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r4.anchor: ويرددون هذا المعنى، وعقبة بن أبي معيط يقول: امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
